sources.title: M. Visser, The Kerr spacetime: A brief introduction, introductory book chapter, arXiv:0706.0622v3 (2008)
sources.locator: Full 41-page PDF fetched and text-inspected. Read sections: §4 Ricci-calculation discussion (PDF p. 12); §5 Boyer-Lindquist coordinates (PDF pp. 14-15); §9 horizons (PDF pp. 24-27); §10 ergospheres (PDF pp. 30-31); §11 Killing vectors (PDF pp. 36-37).

contents.name: §4 Kerr-Schild coordinates and the Ricci-calculation discussion
contents.support: Visser says a direct Ricci calculation in that coordinate representation is costly and recommends another chart; the A-page lemma independently carries out the signed Ricci contraction in the (t, phi, r, u) chart, so the source is context for the route and not a proof substitute.

contents.name: §5 Boyer-Lindquist metric and the a-to-zero Schwarzschild limit
contents.support: Supports the coordinate metric and cross-term convention; the local definition also makes the tensor global at the rotation axis, and the B-page example checks the a=0 limit against the exact Schwarzschild supplier.

contents.name: §9 horizon radii and horizon angular velocity
contents.support: Supports the horizon-root and angular-velocity formulas; the local proof constructs the ingoing metric extension and derives the null normal direction from its inverse metric.

contents.name: §10 stationary-limit surfaces and the ergosphere
contents.support: The source's g(T,T)=0 condition gives the stationary-limit radius; the local proof solves that quadratic and distinguishes the open ergoregion from the horizon.

contents.name: §11 stationary and axial Killing vectors and the horizon generator
contents.support: Supports the two symmetry fields and the form T+Omega_H Phi; the local proof checks both Lie derivatives directly and computes the generator without invoking a rigidity theorem.

source_review.read_extent: The full PDF was fetched; the listed sections and the surrounding metric, horizon, stationary-limit, and Killing-vector derivations were inspected directly.
source_review.supports: Boyer-Lindquist conventions, Schwarzschild limit, horizon and stationary-limit formulas, Killing-field context, and a warning that the Ricci identity needs an actual tensor calculation.
source_review.limitations: The chapter is an introductory survey and explicitly is not exhaustive. Its coordinate singularity discussion is not used as a regularity proof; the local items supply their own global sphere formulation and ingoing extension. Its statement that Kerr is vacuum does not replace the local signed Ricci calculation.

sources.title: H. S. Reall, Black Holes, Part III lecture notes (15 March 2024)
sources.locator: Full 149-page PDF fetched and text-inspected. Read §§7.2-7.6, PDF pp. 93-103: Kerr-Newman context, Kerr metric and ingoing coordinates, maximal extension, geodesic/Hamilton-Jacobi separation, Carter constant, ergosphere, and Penrose process discussion.

contents.name: §7.2 Kerr-Newman charged rotating family
contents.reason: This pair defines and proves properties of the uncharged subextremal Kerr metric; charged Kerr-Newman parameters and electromagnetic field equations are not among its assigned statements or dependencies.

contents.name: §7.3 Kerr metric, horizon, and ingoing coordinates
contents.support: Supports the Kerr coefficients, regular ingoing-chart route, and horizon angular velocity; the local proof performs the coordinate substitution and verifies nondegeneracy and the null generator.

contents.name: §7.4 maximal analytic extension
contents.reason: The assigned claim needs a smooth extension across the outer horizon only; a maximal analytic extension, white-hole region, or additional asymptotic end is not asserted or needed.

contents.name: §7.5 separated geodesic Hamilton-Jacobi equation and Carter separation constant
contents.support: The Reall derivation provides an independent treatment of the separated radial and angular equations; the local theorem recomputes them from the displayed inverse block and proves local branch existence.

contents.name: §7.5 Kerr-specific Killing tensor formula and Carter quadratic integral
contents.reason: The assigned inventory proves the general Killing-tensor conservation mechanism and direct Hamilton-Jacobi separation but does not include a Kerr-specific tensor formula; no such formula or irreducibility claim is made without the regular-frame verification required by the design.

contents.name: §7.6 ergosphere and stationary Killing field
contents.support: Supports the condition g(T,T)>0 in the ergoregion; the local proposition derives the exact stationary-limit root and its axis behavior.

contents.name: §7.6 Penrose process and particle energy extraction
contents.reason: The B-page leaf is a pointwise scalar-stress multiplier calculation, not a particle-splitting model; it makes no extraction, trajectory, or astrophysical energy-transfer claim.

source_review.read_extent: The full lecture-note PDF was fetched; §§7.2-7.6 and their surrounding derivations on PDF pp. 93-103 were inspected directly.
source_review.supports: Kerr metric and horizon coordinates, the local geodesic Hamilton-Jacobi separation calculation, the Carter separation constant context, and the ergosphere condition.
source_review.limitations: The source develops Kerr-Newman before specializing to Kerr and uses geometric units.
